_about: Names for Alley Cat's routines and globals, with the evidence for each.

Third pass on 2026-08-21. Adds the main-loop structure -- attract-mode entry, new-game setup, per-frame body, end-of-room PRNG-driven next-phase pick -- plus the phase dispatch: 8 entries at CS:0x0250 (image 0x7480), reached by `jmp word [cs:bx + 0x250]` in dispatch_current_phase after clamping [current_phase] to 0..7. Individual phase handlers are named by number (phase_0_handler, phase_2_handler, ...) rather than by room because the mapping from phase number to Alley Cat room (birdcage, aquarium, cheese/mice, dog/books, sleeping woman, kittens) is not yet established -- that needs a runtime hook, see knowledge/12. The 158-of-158 style completeness numbers Dam Busters reached are not here yet -- this is early days.

Routine keys are image offsets, the coordinate comrec's labels use (5-digit hex, e.g. 0x0CD51 for L_0CD51). Global keys are DS-relative offsets, the numbers that appear inside brackets in the .asm -- because Alley Cat is a multi-segment MZ that sets DS := 0x0010 at boot, DS-relative offset 0x0690 is physical image offset 0x0790, but annotate.py matches the bracketed operand verbatim.
Getting the two coordinate systems the wrong way round is the mistake that costs a session, and the only symptom is silence.

0x07230: MZ entry from mzinfo (CS:IP = 0723:0000 -> image 0x7230). Pushes DS:0 as a far return address for eventual return-to-DOS, calls startup_video_probe, loads DS := 0x0010 (the one distinct segment value in the relocation table), reads the machine ID, initialises the keyboard subsystem, sets CGA mode 4 (INT 10h AH=0), applies the palette, seeds the PRNG, sets sound_enabled := 0xFF, then falls into attract_loop_start
0x072B1: outer loop entry, reached from entry and from every path that requests attract mode (main_state := 0 falls back here). Calls L_098C0 (candidate high-score-promote -- 7-byte state at [0x1F82] copied to [0x1F89] if greater), then zeros the phase_history_index at [8] and the current_phase at [4]
0x072C0: attract-mode frame body. apply_palette, speaker_off, blit_title_frame (L_0CEE0), speaker_off; if [0x41A] is zero (never-been-attracted-yet latch) drops through attract_show_title_and_wait once, then falls into new_game_setup
0x072D3: one-shot attract branch: speaker_off, calls L_0D115 (a wait-for-key screen that clear_cga_screens then loops on key_tick_counter and the message-list step), and latches [0x41A] := 1 so subsequent attract iterations skip the wait
0x072DE: resets the per-game state before entering a level. Copies attract_history_word ([0x6DF8]) into [8] (phase_history_index), sets main_state := 3 (playing), zeros [0x1C30], captures INT 1Ah tick DX into startup_time_low, zeros the four game-state flags ([0x414], [0x418]..[0x41C], [0x41B]). If main_state got cleared during this, goes back to attract_loop_start; otherwise checks the two restart flags [0x41B] and [0x41C]. Falls into game-init calls (L_09C30, L_0C630) then apply_palette / init_sound_state (L_0CAED) etc., then game_frame_top
0x07385: top of the game-play frame loop. If main_state is zero, jumps back to attract_loop_start; else calls the keyboard-event observer L_08568, and if either restart flag ([0x41C] request_attract, [0x41B] request_new_game) is set, jumps back to the matching setup
0x073A6: per-frame body inside the game-play loop. Calls the delta-tick + joystick sampler L_08430, then L_07B15 (unnamed per-frame update) and L_09093 (unnamed per-frame update). If [0x1CB8] is zero, applies a 1-in-4 frame throttle via inc [frame_throttle_counter] / test & 3 -- 3 out of 4 frames skip the expensive draw block that follows
0x073E7: reached when the current phase exits (any of [0x551], [0x553], [0x41B], [0x41C] non-zero). Captures INT 1Ah tick DX into end_of_level_tick; copies the player position ([0x579] -> [1], [0x57B] -> [3]); latches game_session_active := 1. If [0x418] is set, forces current_phase := 7 (and clears [0x418]); else picks the next phase via PRNG: `test dl, 0xA0 / je uniform` -- 75% weighted table lookup, 25% uniform. Weighted: bx := (phase_history_index & 3) * 4 + (PRNG & 3), al := [bx + phase_select_table_weighted]. Uniform: dx := PRNG & 7, reject if >= 5, al := [dx + phase_select_table_uniform]. Then rejects the new phase if it matches phase_history_last -- and if it also matches phase_history_prev, retries the whole selection; otherwise commits and shifts the two-slot history
0x07468: zeros [6], reads bx := current_phase; if > 7 clamps to 0; `shl bx, 1 / jmp word [cs:bx + 0x250]` -- indirect jump through phase_dispatch_table at CS:0x0250 (image 0x7480). This is the game's phase selector
0x07490: phase 7 entry (highest dispatch slot, offset 0x260 -> image 0x7490). Two structural anomalies mark it as NOT a normal gameplay phase: its exit OR is `[0x551] | [0x553] | [0x41C] | [0x41B]` (missing 0x552, the level-end flag every other phase watches), and it does not call the per-frame updates L_09093 / L_0A380 that the gameplay phases share. Init sequence: screen_transition_wipe / init_phase_screen_pattern / set_cat_position_for_phase / init_gameplay_state / init_object_slot_32XX / phase_7_init_a (L_0D330, sets [0x70F2]=0) / init_phase_7_state (L_0C189, sets up state at 0x4548..0x45B6 with a PRNG-picked value). Per-frame: handle_keyboard_events, poll_joystick_or_delay, update_speaker_sweep, movement_tick_scheduler, phase_7_animated_sprite (L_0D336), L_0A196, L_0A090, L_0BE40. This is most likely the game-over / scoreboard screen
0x074DA: phase 6 entry (offset 0x2AA -> image 0x74DA). Distinct from all other phases in one way: its per-frame update BRANCHES on `[0x1CB8]` (a gameplay-active gate) -- when zero, calls L_0A380; when non-zero, calls L_09093. Every other phase always calls both. Init: transition + phase_init trio + init_phase_6_state_noop (L_0BE30, single `ret` -- phase 6 has no state to init). Per-frame: standard core plus phase_6_tick_b (L_0BB73) and phase_6_tick_a (L_0BA06). Exit OR includes all five triggers (0x551, 0x552, 0x553, 0x41B, 0x41C)
0x0752E: phase 5 entry (offset 0x2FE -> image 0x752E). Standard init + init_phase_5_state (L_0B7AA, sets up position at (0x90, 0x86) and state at 0x40A8..0x40C8). Per-frame: standard core plus phase_5_tick_b (L_0B7DB) and phase_5_tick_a (L_0B570). Normal exit OR
0x07579: phase 4 entry (offset 0x349 -> image 0x7579). Init: standard trio then init_phase_4_actors (L_0B2C0, initializes 4 actor slots at 0x3EAE..0x3EDA with random offsets). Per-frame: standard core plus phase_4_tick_a (L_0B0C0) and phase_4_tick_b (L_0B2F2). Normal exit OR
0x075C4: phase 3 entry (offset 0x394 -> image 0x75C4). Init: standard trio then init_phase_3_state_a (L_0AD60, inits [0x37AF..0x37B4]) then init_phase_3_state_b (L_0AEC0, inits [0x3964..0x396D]). Per-frame: standard core plus phase_3_tick_a (L_0AEE1) and phase_3_tick_b (L_0AD72). Normal exit OR
0x0AD60: zero-inits and seeds the first phase-3 state block: `[0x37AF]` := 3, then `[0x37B0]`, `[0x37B2]`, `[0x37B4]` := 1. Called from phase_3_handler init
0x0AEC0: initializes the second phase-3 state block: `[0x3966]` := 8, `[0x396A]` := 1, `[0x3967]` := 0, `[0x396D]` := 2, `[0x3964]` := 0x0118, `[0x396B]` := 0. Called from phase_3_handler init
0x0B2C0: 4-slot loop initializing phase-4 actors. For each slot bx (0..3): `[bx + 0x3EAE]` := 1, `[bx + 0x3EB2]` := 0, calls L_0B4A7 (per-slot helper), picks PRNG value dl, `dl = (dl & 0xF) + 0x14`, stores at `[bx + 0x3EB6]`. Zeros `[0x3EDA]` after the loop. The four actors are almost certainly the moving objects of phase 4 -- given Alley Cat's rooms, likely the mice in the cheese room or the birds in the birdcage
0x0B7AA: initializes the phase-5 layout: sets `[0x40A8]` := 0x90 (col), `[0x40AA]` := 0x86 (row), computes CGA offset via cga_row_col_to_offset and stores at `[0x40AB]`, calls L_0B989 (sprite prep?), then zero-inits `[0x40AF]`, `[0x40B1]`, `[0x40B8]`, sets `[0x40B9]` := 1 and `[0x40C8]` := 0xFF
0x0BE30: single `ret` -- phase_6_handler calls this in its init slot but the phase has no state to initialize. Present so the phase's init sequence has the same shape as the others
0x0C189: zero-inits and seeds phase-7 state. Zeros `[0x45B6]`; PRNG-picks dx, masks to 0..0x7F, adds 0x60, stores at `[0x4548]`. Various flags at `[0x454A]` := 0, `[0x454E]` := 1, `[0x4551]` := 0, `[0x4553]` := 0. Reads INT 1Ah tick, stores in `[0x45B4]` (approx)
0x0D330: single-byte init: `[0x70F2]` := 0. Called from phase_7_handler init. Likely a shared flag between phase_7_handler's frame body and phase_7_animated_sprite (L_0D336), which zeros the same byte on the non-drawn branch
0x0D336: rate-limited to once per BIOS tick change (`cmp dx, [0x70EE]`). When the tick moves, calls L_0D4D6 -- if the return CF says 'draw', does the classic sprite-flicker cycle: restore_video_from_snapshot (erase the old frame) / L_0D45B (advance sprite/position) / sprite_draw_saving_bg (paint the new one). Zero `[0x70F2]` on the erase path. This is an animated sprite in phase 7 (the game-over screen)
0x0AD72: phase-3 per-frame tick, rate-limited by comparing INT 1Ah tick DX to `[0x37B8]`. When the tick moves, sets `[0x37B8]` := DX and `[0x37B6]` := 4, then does phase-3-specific work. Caller: phase_3_handler inner loop only
0x0AEE1: phase-3 per-frame tick, rate-limited to 2+ BIOS ticks against `[0x39C8]`. Caller: phase_3_handler inner loop only. Distinct state block from phase_3_tick_a
0x0B0C0: phase-4 per-frame update. Caller: phase_4_handler inner loop only
0x0B2F2: phase-4 per-frame update, distinct from phase_4_tick_a. Caller: phase_4_handler inner loop only
0x0B570: phase-5 per-frame update. Caller: phase_5_handler inner loop only
0x0B7DB: phase-5 per-frame update, distinct from phase_5_tick_a. Caller: phase_5_handler inner loop only
0x0BA06: phase-6 per-frame update. Caller: phase_6_handler inner loop only
0x0BB73: phase-6 per-frame update. Caller: phase_6_handler inner loop only
0x0BE40: phase-7 per-frame update, rate-limited against `[0x45B8]`. Advances `[0x45B6]` counter (increments, then dispatches on specific values 1 and 4). Caller: phase_7_handler inner loop only
0x0A090: phase-7 per-frame update. Caller: phase_7_handler inner loop only
0x0A196: phase-7 per-frame update. Caller: phase_7_handler inner loop only
0x08DAA: collision test between an object drawn during attract mode and the cat sprite. Only fires when `[current_phase] == 0` (i.e. during the outer attract loop where main_loop zeros [4] just before dispatch) AND `[0x1673]` is non-zero. Calls boxes_overlap (L_0A059) with rectangle (`[0x1671]`, `[0x1673]`, `[0x17DF]`) vs the cat's (`[0x579]`, `[0x57B]`, 10, 8). CF-based branch on overlap
0x09093: per-frame internal counter advance, called from every phase handler. Reads INT 1Ah tick; runs only if the delta from `[scheduler_last_tick]` (0x1CC9) is >= 1+([scheduler_counter] & 1), so alternates between 1-tick and 2-tick thresholds. Also gates on check_cga_vretrace_bit -- skips if not in vretrace. When it fires: updates scheduler_last_tick, increments scheduler_counter, decrements `[0x1CC1]` if non-zero (which triggers speaker_off and phase-transition writes when it hits zero)
0x09325: detects when the cat has reached a specific bottom-of-screen trigger area. Guarded on `[sound_gate_flag]` (0x1CB8) == 0 AND at least one of `[0x1CBF] | [0x1CC0] | [0x1CC1]` set. Requires cat_row >= 0xA3 (near bottom of the 320x200 screen), `[0x558]` == 0, and cat_col in range `[[0x1CC6] - 0x38 .. [0x1CC6] + 0x20]` (a ~90-pixel horizontal band). On match, calls L_09366 -- this is the trigger for the cat's fence-to-window jump animation
0x09B88: stores AX at [0x2634], then calls blit_sprite_list 4 times with BX loaded from a 4-entry pointer table at [0x2636..0x263C] (loop SI = 8 down by 2 until 0). Renders 4 composed sprites in sequence
0x09BA0: same shape as blit_sprite_lists_4x but calls blit_sprite_list 5 times from a pointer table starting at [0x263E..0x2646] (loop SI = 0xA down by 2)
0x09BD0: blits one sprite list at [0x251C] then clears three 0x24-word (72-byte) horizontal strips in CGA video RAM at offsets `[0x267E] + 0x284`, `+ 0x1184`, and `+ 0x2284` -- likely the trailing/blanking columns behind a moving sprite so its old positions get erased
0x09EFC: colored-sprite blit for CGA mode 4 (2 bits per pixel). Same width/height cache pattern as blit_cga_interleaved but with per-pixel masking: for each byte, reads current video at ES:DI, saves at DS:BP, loads sprite word from DS:SI, then does bit-manipulation with masks 0x30C0/0xFF0 to combine the sprite color pattern with the underlying video. The most-called unnamed blitter (12 sites); it is the routine that draws animated color sprites
0x0CD93: guarded on `sound_enabled`; every 2+ BIOS ticks (delta from `[0x59C0]` >= 2), advances a sound counter at `[0x59BE]`. When the counter's masked value reaches 0x86, does phase-specific sound state updates. Called from many per-frame updates -- this is the beat-clock for the sound engine
0x0D42A: renders a specific sprite in phase_7 (the game-over screen). Selects sprite by `([0x70F0] & 0x1E0) + 0x6F30`, with a 0xC0-byte offset when `[0x70F6] == 0xFF` (alternate frame). Draws to CGA video at `[0x70FA]` using scratch at `[0x70CC]`, dimensions 8x2. Companion to restore_phase_7_sprite_bg
0x0D45B: restores the background behind the phase-7 sprite. Guarded on `[0x70F7]` == 0. Blits from scratch at `[0x70CC]` to CGA video at `[0x70F8]` via blit_cga_interleaved. Called by phase_7_animated_sprite between erase and redraw
0x076D0: periodic spawner. Decrements `[0x531]`; when it reaches zero (once per period) tries to spawn: increments back to 1, gates on check_cga_vretrace_bit, requires `[0x55A]` == 0 and `[0x1673]` == 0 (spawn slot empty), then reads INT 1Ah tick and checks it differs from `[0x544]` to serialize. Chooses a spawn type by indexing `[bx + 0x532]` where bx = phase_history_index, then reads more state at [0x52F] and calls L_07888
0x07863: 5-iteration rotate-through-carry-RIGHT of the byte at `[bx + 0x1016]` where bx = `[0x52F] + [table@0x541]`. `lahf/sahf` around it preserves the shift's carry bit across the loop. If the table entry is 9, jumps to shift_sprite_column_rcl (L_0787E) which does the opposite direction. This is pixel-column scrolling on a saved sprite buffer
0x0787E: opposite direction of shift_sprite_column_rcr: `rcl byte [bx + 0x1016], 1` in a loop with `lahf/sahf` carry preservation. dec bx per iteration (walks backward through the buffer). Reached from shift_sprite_column_rcr when the direction table holds 9
0x07888: range check on cat_row_plus_50 against a per-object table at `[bx + 0x53A..0x53D]`. Sets flag byte `[0x4D6]` := 1 if cat is inside the zone AND `[0x55C]` >= 1, else 0
0x078AD: draws a randomized speaker/mouth animation pattern: fills 0x20 words (64 bytes) at ES:DI with 0xAAAA, patches 4 bytes at +4..+7 with 0x4444, then uses PRNG to choose a variation. Called for the cat's meow/talk animation
0x0790E: picks a random pointer from a 4-entry table at `[bx + 0x4D0]`. PRNG-picks a 3-bit value; if it lands on 6 returns AL=0 (a null pick), otherwise reads word from `[bx + dx + 0x4D0]` and loops through 8 lodsw operations. bx is the caller's context
0x07930: 3-instruction routine: zeros movement_last_tick (0x57D) and movement_countdown (0x684). Called to reset the cat's movement timing at phase transitions
0x0793D: initializes the cat's starting position on entering a new game. If saved cat_col `[0x579]` is < 0xA0 (left half of screen), cat starts at col=0 facing right (direction ah=1). Else cat starts at col=0x128 facing left (direction ah=0xFF). Sets movement direction `[0x56E]`, animation frame `[0x558]` := 3, frame timer `[0x559]` := 0xC, row := 0xB4 (row 180, near bottom of the 320x200 screen). Then computes the CGA offset via cga_row_col_to_offset, stores in sprite_dst_offset, and sets sprite_width_cache := 0xB03
0x07AA2: starts a meow-style sound effect. Sets speaker_pit_divisor := 0x400 (a specific pitch). If `[0x584]` is non-zero, returns without playing (already meowing?). Otherwise sets sound duration counter `[0x576]` := 8, chooses pitch direction based on cat row vs `[0x2652]` -- the cat has a different meow when on top of vs below a reference row
0x081F9: picks horizontal movement bounds for the current phase. Default: `[0x5F6]` := 8 (left bound), `[0x5F8]` := 0x123 (right bound). For phase 7 (game-over screen): `[0x5F6]` := 0x24, `[0x5F8]` := 0x10F -- narrower bounds. Then computes movement clamping based on cat_col, direction `[0x56E]`, and step size `[0x572]`
0x08F9E: the PCjr palette-set primitive called 3x by apply_palette on PCjr. `mov ax, 0x1000 / int 10h` -- INT 10h AH=10h AL=00h with BL = palette register index (1/2/3) and BH = color. `push si / pop si` preserves the caller's palette-selector index
0x0994E: adds two 7-digit BCD numbers (score arithmetic). Loops CX=7 down; for each digit reads [bx+di] and [bx+si], does `adc + aaa` (add with carry + ASCII adjust for addition, i.e. BCD add), stores back at [bx+di]. `pushf/popf` preserves the carry between iterations. Classic 8088 multi-digit BCD adder
0x08B52: one-shot sprite blit for an object whose destination is [0x17E5], source is fixed at 0x17EE, and width comes from [0x17E3]. ES:=B800, then blit_cga_interleaved. Likely an attract-mode or menu object
0x08D35: boxes_overlap test between an object at (col [0x1666], row [0x1668]) with dims (0x20, 0x18) and the cat at (cat_col, cat_row) with dims (0xE, 0xF). CF-based return per boxes_overlap
0x09311: sprite blit for an object at [0x1CBD] with source 0x1C40 and width from [0x1CC2]. Same shape as blit_object_at_17E5 but different addresses; likely a gameplay object drawn at variable position
0x0992C: calls L_09969 (a 7-byte compare+copy helper) with bx=0x1F82 (candidate score) and di=0x143C (destination). Related to the maybe-promote-high-score pattern -- another `if score > record: copy 7 bytes`. Reached from new_game_setup
0x09CF6: multi-pass sprite drawer with state at [0x2AC4] (pass counter) and [0x2AC9] (bh cache). Loops indexing [bx + 0x2ABA] where bx = phase_history_index. Called from screen-setup paths
0x09DA1: repeated sprite draw stepping DI by 0x14 (20 bytes) each iteration. Sets [0x2AC4] := 4 as iteration count. Source = 0x2680 with dims 0x1005 = width 5 words, height 0x10 rows. Stripe/pattern renderer
0x09527: hit-test guard for objects at [0x1D5C]. If [0x1D59] is zero returns CF=0; else reads packed dims from [0x1D64], swaps halves via `xchg cl, ch`, tests overlap with something. Likely per-mouse or per-actor hit check
0x09252: if [sound_gate_flag] non-zero, returns bh=0. Else increments an input-cycle byte at [0x1CCF], masks with 6 to cycle 4-way, ORs with 8, then dispatches. Runs every frame; likely translates raw key state into gameplay input direction
0x0A569: linked-list traversal: reads bx = [0x327A] (head pointer), follows [bx + 0x3260] as next-pointer, updates head if link is 0 (list ended) and retries from top. On finding a valid link, blits the object from scratch to video via mask-blit at BP=0x31E8, ES=B800, CX=0x1E02
0x0A5D0: erases the phase-1 object at [0x3282] by blitting from scratch at 0x31E8. Guarded on [0x3286] (a 'sprite present' flag). Companion to walk_object_list_head
0x0B989: phase-5-specific sprite draw via sprite_and_mask_blit: BP=0x401E (scratch save), SI=0x3FBE (sprite source), DI=[0x40AB] (dest), CX=0x1003 (dims: width 3 words, height 0x10 rows). Caches DI at [0x40A6] for erase companion
0x0B9A3: erase companion to draw_phase_5_sprite: blits from 0x401E scratch to [0x40A6] cached dest via blit_cga_interleaved
0x0BD33: erases the phase-6 sprite at [0x43DE] by restoring from scratch at 0x43A0. Guarded on [0x43E0] (a 'sprite present' flag)
0x0BDF8: picks a sprite frame from a per-index table at [bx + 0x44C4], multiplies the index by 32 (`shl 5`) to compute an offset into the sprite bank starting at 0x41FC, and blits to video via blit_cga_interleaved. CX=0x802 dims (2 words wide, 8 rows tall)
0x0C17A: conditional draw of a second phase-7 sprite: if [0x454E] is zero returns; else loads DI from [0x454C] and calls L_0C238 (the actual drawer)
0x0C290: clamps cat_col to <= 0x116 (max screen col), then subtracts 0x10 to compute a related position. Called from L_0C4BB during the boot / reset path
0x0C37A: 3-iteration loop copying from source blocks at 0x4DA4/0x4DAA into [0x4D6A]. Sets up per-round bonus data or similar during boot
0x0C4BB: one step of the boot/intro sequence: calls sound_delay_start, sets CGA palette (INT 10h AH=0Bh BX=0x101), then chains through L_0C290 / L_0C37A / L_0CDEF, and increments [main_state] if it is below 9. Advances the intro/attract animation one step at a time
0x0C500: a second PIT-ch2 pattern stepper (distinct from advance_pit_pattern_step). Guards on sound_enabled and 1-tick BIOS-tick rate limit ([0x52C4]). Cycles through a table at 0x52CA indexed by [0x52C6] advancing by 2 each firing; silences speaker when the picked value matches the terminator at [0x52C8]. Plays a melody phrase, not a repeating 4-note pattern
0x0C99E: blocking beep like beep_blocking but with a fixed CX=0x1000 iteration count (halved on standard PC via `shr cx, 1`) and divisor from [0x5ACB]. Used for a specific boot/intro chime rather than as a general primitive
0x0C9D6: boot-animation timer: increments byte [0x5ACF], and every 0x40 ticks (when the low 6 bits wrap) also increments word [0x5ACD]. Then computes bl from ([0x5ACD] >> 2) & 0x1F and compares against the byte counter, setting a decision value in dl (0 or 2). Drives the intro-screen pacing
0x0CB8D: plays a random-pitch tone as an SFX. Guarded on sound_enabled and sfx_playing_state==0 (no other SFX active). PRNG-picks a byte, masks to 0..0x7F, adds 0xAA to compute BX (duration param), then adds 0x1E to compute AX (frequency), calls sfx_start_tone. Frequencies range 0xC8..0x147 -- percussion/noise range; probably the random meow
0x0CBAF: plays a sweeping tone effect. Guarded on sound_enabled. Adds [0x5B08] (a sweep phase) to 0x1200 and 0x1312 to compute AX (freq) and BX (param), advances [0x5B08] by 0x15E, then calls sfx_start_tone. Each call produces a slightly higher pitch than the last -- a rising melody
0x0CDEF: spins on advance_sound_timer until the sound counter [0x59BE] reaches 0x7C. Guarded on sound_enabled (returns immediately if muted). Called from the intro/boot path to wait for a specific sound phase before proceeding
0x0CECE: wrapper for bios_print_string that first ensures DS := 0x10 (the data segment). Called by startup_video_probe which momentarily sets DS to video (0xB800) for the memory test and then needs to print the failure message from data
0x0D06B: 2-slot cyclic background pattern: advances counter [0x6A8D] by 2, masks with 2 (giving 0/2 = 2 slots), picks source pointer from `[bx + 0x6A8F]`, blits pattern of dims 0xC0A (width 0xA words, height 0xC rows) to CGA video at 0x1D38. Half the size of cycle_phase_1_bg_pattern's 4-slot version
0x0D4D6: decision routine for phase_7_animated_sprite: if [0x70F2] is zero returns CF=0 (skip draw); else builds a bounding box from ([0x70F3], [0x70F5]) with dims (0x10, 0x18) and boxes_overlap-tests it against the cat at (cat_col, cat_row) with dims (0x18, ...). CF-based return

0x08608: reads port 0x3DA (CGA status) and masks bit 3 -- the vertical retrace flag. Returns non-zero while the beam is in vertical retrace
0x08618: fills 22 bytes at DS:[key_state_table] with 0x80 (the 'released' bit), and caches BIOS byte 40h:0012h into cs:[saved_bios_kb_flags]. Called from entry once before install_keyboard_handler

Blits each entry with `rep movsb` per row and the same 0x2000-XOR / +0x50 interleave handling as blit_cga_interleaved

AL = DL * 40; on odd rows adds 0x1FD8 to reach the second interleaved bank (even scanlines at 0x0000..0x1FFF, odd at 0x2000..0x3FFF); AX += CX >> 2; CL = (CX & 3) << 1. Called 28 times, always immediately before a sprite draw

For each word: reads current ES:[DI], stores it at DS:[BP] (the scratch save), loads a sprite word from DS:SI, computes (sprite AND current), writes back to ES:[DI]. Each row is a `rep movsw`, then `xor di, 0x2000` flips to the other bank; when the flip lands in the low bank it adds 0x50 to advance to the next visible scanline pair

Exists because one caller (snapshot_video_rect) sets DS := 0xB800 (video, as source) and ES := 0x0010 (data, as destination), swapping the usual segment roles -- so the cache access has to go through ES to reach the data segment

0x0A040: reads PIT channel 0 counter (same latch dance as read_pit_counter), and if the reading came back zero substitutes 0xFA59 as a fallback seed. Called once from entry immediately after the video mode is set
0x0A059: 2D bounding-box overlap test on two rectangles: (AX..BX, DL..DH) versus (SI..DI, CL..CH). Returns CF=1 if the boxes overlap, CF=0 otherwise. Handles the classic wrap case (`sub ax, di / jae ... / sub ax, ax`) so a negative delta is clamped to zero before the ordering compare

0x0CB6B: starts a speaker sound effect. Guarded on sound_enabled -- returns immediately if muted. Programs PIT ch2 mode 3 with divisor from BX, gates the speaker on, then spins `loop L_0CBF5` for CX iterations (halved via `shr cx, 1` on standard PC because it runs faster than PCjr), then calls speaker_off. Only used from places where blocking is fine

On success prints the sign-on string at DS:0x60F0, patches the BIOS 40h:0010h video-mode nibble to CGA 40x25 color, and sets INT 10h mode 4 (CGA 320x200). On failure prints the error string at DS:0x6112 and enters an infinite `jmp $` at L_0CECC. If bits 4-5 are anything else the routine returns immediately, leaving the CGA mode-4 switch that the entry does via INT 10h AH=4 as the only path

0x0D08B: INT 10h AH=2 (set cursor position) with column = 0, page = 0, row = DH (as passed in). Sets the BIOS text cursor to the start of the given row
0x0D1E1: prints one entry from the parallel message tables. Reads bx := message_index, DX := word [bx + message_row_table] (cursor row), calls bios_set_cursor_row; then SI := word [bx + message_string_table] (string pointer), calls bios_print_string; advances message_index by 2
0x0D1FD: fills both interleaved banks of CGA video memory with zeros: 0xB800:0000..0x1F3F (rep stosw with CX=0xFA0 = 4000 words = 8000 bytes) then 0xB800:2000..0x3F3F likewise. 16000 bytes total -- the full CGA mode-4 framebuffer

Tested at the top of nearly every sound routine (25 references) -- if zero, the routine returns without touching the speaker

0x0003: byte version of the player's row position ([0x57B]) copied here by end_of_room_pick_next
0x0004: the game's current phase (0..7), used as the index into phase_dispatch_table by dispatch_current_phase. Zeroed at attract_loop_start; set by end_of_room_pick_next after a PRNG pick; re-asserted by each phase handler at its entry (`mov word [4], N`) in case that handler was entered outside the dispatch path

0x057D: 16-bit INT 1Ah tick cached by movement_tick_scheduler. When the current tick differs from this, the scheduler fires
0x05D9: 8-entry, 16-word table (16 bytes) of the cat's starting column for each phase. Indexed by `bx*2` where bx = current_phase, read by set_cat_position_for_phase
0x05E9: 8-entry byte table of the cat's starting row for each phase. Indexed by `bx` where bx = current_phase, read by set_cat_position_for_phase
0x0684: 16-bit countdown decremented by movement_tick_scheduler on each same-tick call. Reset to 0x20 (0x10 on PCjr) each time the tick advances. When it reaches zero, triggers a movement update
0x1832: current column of the iris wipe being drawn by draw_transition_iris
0x1834: current row of the iris wipe
0x1835: current radius (in row-pairs) of the iris wipe -- grows outward each iteration
0x1837: how many rows per iteration draw_transition_iris fills (initialised to 8 by screen_transition_wipe)
0x1839: 16-bit fill pattern used by draw_transition_iris. Zeroed on first pass, then set to 0xAAAA or 0x5555 (phase-specific) on the second pass
0x1CB8: byte gating update_speaker_sweep. When zero, the sweep is inhibited
0x1CC9: 16-bit last INT 1Ah tick cached by L_09093 (the per-frame scheduler)
0x1CE1: 16-bit counter incremented by L_09093 each firing; its low bit alternates the tick-delta threshold between 1 and 2
0x5B0F: byte gating the alternate branch of update_speaker_sweep. Non-zero puts the sweep into a decrement-per-tick mode instead of the freq-sweep
0x5B10: 16-bit INT 1Ah tick cached by update_speaker_sweep for delta detection
0x5B12: 16-bit divisor being swept downward by update_speaker_sweep. Each firing: divisor = (this & 0x1FF) + 0xC8, then this -= 0x4B -- a falling tone
0x069A: byte cached by poll_joystick_or_delay from port 0x201 bit 4 (the fire button). 0x10 = pressed, 0 = released

0x069F: 16-bit INT 1Ah tick cached by poll_joystick_or_delay for its 2-tick rate limit
0x328C: 16-bit tick shadow for phase_1_object_tick. Rate-limits the object's animation to whatever interval `[bx + 0x32F2]` holds for the current phase
0x32EA: byte animation step for the phase-1 object at 0x328E. Incremented by phase_1_object_tick when the tick delta exceeds the phase-specific threshold. init_object_slot_32XX seeds it to 0x6C
0x35D8: byte index into bg_pattern_table, advanced by cycle_phase_1_bg_pattern by 2 each firing and masked with 6 -- cycles 0/2/4/6/0/2/... through 4 pattern slots
0x35D0: 4-entry table of 16-bit pointers to background pattern blits used by cycle_phase_1_bg_pattern
0x35DA: 16-bit INT 1Ah tick cached by cycle_phase_1_bg_pattern for its 6-tick rate limit

0x041B: byte flag consumed by the main loop: when non-zero, execution jumps back to new_game_setup. Set from deeper game code when a level-end event demands a fresh game session. One of the four values OR'd in each phase handler's exit condition
0x041C: byte flag consumed by the main loop: when non-zero, execution jumps back to attract_show_title_and_wait. Also one of the four values OR'd in each phase handler's exit condition
0x041D: the phase number most recently picked by end_of_room_pick_next. Used to dedup: if the freshly-picked value matches this, the pick is retried
0x041F: the phase number picked before phase_history_last (shifted from it when a new pick commits). Used as the second dedup slot: if the fresh pick matches phase_history_last AND matches this, retry the whole selection
0x0421: 12-byte phase-selection table used 75% of the time by end_of_room_pick_next. Indexed by `bx*4 + dx` where bx = phase_history_index & 3 and dx = (PRNG & 3), so it is 4 rows of 4 entries: given a history bucket, the next phase is picked uniformly from that bucket's four options

_note: Second-pass partition of the 54,555-byte load image on 2026-08-21. 52 spans cover the file with no gap and no overlap; each carries a reason. Every named global's cluster gets its own span; the 22 'unread' spans between them make explicit what has NOT been read as data. The pre-DS zero-fill and the CS code region are single-span for now (the code region will need per-routine partitioning eventually, matching Dam Busters' style).

Keys are IMAGE offsets (base 0x0), not DS-relative like the globals section. Alley Cat's DS is loaded with 0x0010 at boot, so DS-relative offset X = image offset X + 0x0100. When a span reason refers to a global by name, the global's DS-relative address is the same as it appears in the globals section; the physical image offset the span sits at is that value + 0x100. Getting the two coordinate systems mixed is the mistake this file exists to make hard.

Dam Busters has 112 spans covering 65 KB; Alley Cat has 52 covering 54 KB, but most of the DS-segment coverage is still 'unread'. The named clusters here are what has been READ; the unread spans are what remains.
